articles.headline: Falcons to start QB Michael Penix on Thursday vs. Packers
articles.description: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will make his season debut this Thursday night when he starts against the Packers, the team announced Monday.
articles.body:
Michael Penix Jr. will make his season debut in primetime this week, giving the winless Atlanta Falcons much-needed relief at the quarterback position.

The Falcons announced Monday that Penix will start Thursday night on the road against the Green Bay Packers. It will be Penix's first start since Week 11 last November when he tore his left ACL.

Penix had reconstructive surgery a few weeks later and then another procedure to further stabilize the joint. He was cleared by doctors to practice fully in late August but told the team before Week 1 that he was not yet ready for live game action. The typical timetable for a return from ACL surgery is between nine and 12 months.

Tua Tagovailoa, who the Falcons signed in the offseason, got the starting quarterback job out of training camp. But he suffered an oblique injury in practice, forcing third-stringer Cooper Rush into starts in the Falcons' first two games.

Rush, who was also dealing with back spasms, struggled in those games. Rush was 22-of-39 passing for 229 yards with one touchdown, four interceptions and a lost fumble. Rush was benched for undrafted rookie Jack Strand in the third quarter of Sunday's 34-3 loss to the Carolina Panthers.

Strand saw his first action Sunday and threw a pick-six on his first pass attempt. He finished 8-of-15 for 59 yards with no touchdowns and the interception. He was the first quarterback to throw a pick-six in his first career pass attempt since Sam Darnold in 2018 -- and the first Falcons quarterback to do it since Brett Favre in 1991.

Penix, 26, has completed 59.6% of his passes for 2,757 yards with 12 touchdowns and six interceptions over two seasons. He was drafted No. 8 overall by Atlanta in 2024 and replaced Kirk Cousins late in the 2024 season as starter. Penix still only has 12 career starts at quarterback.

articles.headline: NFL: 'No concerns' over field conditions in Rio for Cowboys-Ravens
articles.description: NFL field director Nick Pappas said there are "no concerns right now" over the field conditions for Sunday's game between the Cowboys and Ravens in Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body:
NFL field director Nick Pappas said there are "no concerns right now" about the field conditions in Rio de Janeiro for Sunday's game between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens.

"Look, there's the realities of managing any playing surface and then there's also the realities of managing a grass playing surface that's being used mid-season," Pappas told ESPN on Monday. "So it's all about monitoring it. It's all about having a plan in place and then being able to react to anything that maybe comes our way."

Pappas added, "So what we've seen in Rio is a significant amount of rainfall, a record kind of rainfall over the last six weeks. And that obviously poses challenges just from a management perspective, but nothing that we're not capable of managing or prepared to take."

Asked if there has been any talk about moving the game, Pappas said, "No, that's not a conversation."

Questions about the quality of the playing surface at Rio's Maracanã Stadium started last week, when professional soccer players voiced complaints about their home stadium's grass field.

"It's unbelievable that we're playing on a field like this," Flamengo Football Club goalkeeper Agustin Rossi said, according to AtoZ Sports. "If you look at it, there are bumps everywhere. There's still going to be an NFL game here during the international break. After that game, I hope the field is in better shape."

The Cowboys and Ravens are both flying in on Thursday night and practicing in Brazil on Friday.

Asked about the Ravens' concern level over the field, Ravens coach Minter said, "It's really in the league's hands and I think we've been in contact with them. They got people there, feel pretty good about it. So both teams are going to be playing there and we'll be ready to roll."

After Dallas' 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders on Sunday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said, "I trust that the league's going to make the right decision and they'll get the field up to standard."

This marks the NFL's third game in Brazil but first in Rio. In the league's first game in South America in 2024, a number of players for the Eagles and Packers lost their footing during the game and later attributed it to the slick surface at Corinthians Arena in São Paulo.

The most extreme circumstance came in 2018, when the NFL moved the Chiefs-Rams game from Mexico City to the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum because of poor field conditions at Estadio Azteca.

"I know that's of utmost concern to the league that the teams have good playing service down there," Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said Sunday. "So well obviously, you'll certainly stay informed as we look to it."

ESPN's Todd Archer contributed to this report

articles.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Dalton Schultz, Jonah Coleman highlight top options for Week 3
articles.description: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.
articles.body:
Each Monday, before the current NFL week ends, we will identify players worthy of your attention available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues. Things change quickly for player valuation and roles each week in the NFL, and free agency is a critical way to acquire players. We are here to help!

Top pickup options at every position

Looking for the top recommendation at each skill position? Look no further! Here are the players to target heading into Week 3, along with their current roster percentages and a recommendation of how much of your free agent budget (FAB) you should consider using for your bid. 

Tyler Shough, QB, Saints (rostered in 49.7% of leagues, 10-15% of your FAB)

Last week's most recommended QB remains available in barely more than half of ESPN's standard leagues, though likely not for long after yet another solid performance (22.38 points) in a road win against the mighty Baltimore Ravens. This week, the New Orleans Saints host the unbeaten Las Vegas Raiders. Ignore the records. It's a positive matchup. Shough looks like more than a streamer, too, especially since the NFC South doesn't exactly feature top defensive teams and the Saints haven't played any division games yet.

Jonah Coleman, RB, Broncos (15.2% rostered, 10-12% FAB)

Starter J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) wasn't doing so much when he left the game in the second half, having scored just 3.6 points, and rookie Coleman helped spark the offense with his 14.8 points, including a touchdown run. Coleman, a fourth-round pick from Washington, barely played in Week 1, but now he might be his team's starter for this week against the Los Angeles Rams -- pending the status of Dobbins and RJ Harvey (also a hamstring issue) -- and perhaps beyond.

 Denzel Boston, WR, Browns (26.4%, 8-10% FAB):

The rookie Boston scored a touchdown in a blowout Week 1 loss. It was nice, but not really a reason to trust him in Week 2. Then he scored another TD on Sunday. Now, he is quite intriguing, even considering Cleveland's QB situation. Boston is averaging 22 yards per reception through two games. If you wish to invest in a Browns receiver, Boston is the top option over fellow rookie KC Concepcion (57.6%) and the quite invisible Jerry Jeudy (22.1%).

Dalton Schultz, TE, Texans (21.3%, 2% FAB):

Schultz was the main (and perhaps only) beneficiary of the Nico Collins (hamstring) injury, catching 12 passes for 140 yards and achieving 26 fantasy points. No other member of the Houston Texans reached six catches or 40 receiving yards. We really shouldn't be so surprised, though. Schultz ended last season with 82 receptions -- tied for third among tight ends -- and 10th at the position in fantasy points. He might lack the upside of other top tight ends, but his is a relatively high floor, whether Collins plays or not.

Other quarterbacks

Jordan Love, Packers (44.7%, 10% FAB): Love is a bit more rostered now than he was last week, and those who relied on him enjoyed a modest 13.8 fantasy points Sunday

articles.headline: Hawks rookie Henri Veesaar (ACL) expected to miss season
articles.description: Hawks rookie 7-footer Henri Veesaar suffered a torn ACL in his right knee during a workout last week and is expected to miss the season.
articles.body:
Atlanta Hawks rookie center Henri Veesaar is expected to miss the 2026-27 season after tearing the ACL in his right knee.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15 and will undergo surgery in October. The 7-foot center was drafted with the 52nd overall pick by the LA Clippers and was traded to Atlanta.

Veesaar, 22, averaged 17 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.2 blocks and 42.6% 3-point shooting in 31 starts for North Carolina during his senior season.

The Hawks also announced they signed guard Isaac McKneely, who averaged 6.7 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 18.9 minutes during Atlanta's two summer leagues.

articles.headline: Packers WR Reed sustained back, not neck injury, source says
articles.description: Packers receiver Jayden Reed actually sustained a back injury - and not a neck injury as originally thought - in Sunday's game against the Jets and was expected to return to Green Bay on Monday, a sourced told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Packers receiver Jayden Reed actually suffered a back injury -- and not a neck injury as originally thought -- in Sunday's game against the New York Jets and was expected to return to Green Bay on Monday, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Reed was taken from MetLife Stadium to a nearby hospital and did not travel home with the team after its 20-17 overtime win. He was injured on the Packers' second play from scrimmage after he caught a 4-yard pass in the left flat. New York's Demario Davis turned Reed sideways with a tackle attempt and then fellow Jets defender Kingsley Enagbare caught Reed in the back/next area with a glancing blow.

The game was delayed for several minutes while medical personnel from both teams attended to Reed. He was eventually placed on a backboard and had a strap over his helmet to stabilize his head and neck before he was placed on the cart and driven off the field.

The Packers announced during the game that Reed had a neck injury, and then after the game coach Matt LaFleur said Reed was able to move all of his extremities.

The 26-year-old Reed signed a three-year, $50.25 million contract extension in April.

One play after Reed was injured, the Packers lost right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele to a right knee injury that LaFleur said was believed to be a significant injury. Bako-Bewele was expected to undergo further testing on Monday.

The Packers (1-1) have a short turnaround for Thursday's home opener against the Atlanta Falcons.

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Kyler Murray returns for Vikings, brings matchup upside vs. Bucs
articles.description: The Minnesota Vikings have announced that Kyler Murray will start on Sunday, but how much upside does the QB have?
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 21: Kyler Murray clears protocol, will start Week 3

By Michael F. Florio

Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol and will start in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. We have not seen much Murray in a Vikings uniform, but he brings QB1 upside due to his rushing ability and the matchup.

The Bucs have allowed 234 passing yards per game, which ranks 11th highest in the NFL. That is after allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the NFL in 2025. Last week they allowed 19.72 fantasy points to Deshaun Watson, 11th-best among QBs through Sunday.

Murray was a fantasy target of mine this summer due to him being in the best system of his career, with great pass catchers around him. He has been top 12 in fantasy points per game among QBs in every year but one of his career. That is largely due to his rushing ability and highlights the safe floor that he brings.

Some QBs I would start him over in Week 3 are Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Baker Mayfield and Jordan Love.

Which Commanders should you start with Daniels out?

Marcus Mariota is expected to start Week 3 for the Washington Commanders as Jayden Daniels continues to seek opinions on his dislocated left elbow. Daniels does not have a timetable as of now.

Mariota started eight games for the Commanders last season, averaging 200 passing yards and 32 rushing yards per game. He threw 10 touchdowns and added another with his legs.

Mariota is not someone that fantasy managers should be looking to force into their lineups. He is more an option for those in Superflex leagues who now find themselves in a pinch. He brings a safer floor than you may expect, due to the rushing numbers, but falls far short of Daniels' ceiling.

The Commanders face the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3, so even those in superflex leagues should look in another direction to help replace Daniels in their starting lineup. I would also recommend trying to avoid the Commanders' pass catchers in this one. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs remain the top options, but are more "boom-or-bust" WR3 or flex plays.

Mariota did throw four times to each McLaurin and Dyami Brown in Week 2. He threw three times to Diggs, but the duo did connect for a touchdown.

NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Sept. 21

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"

Free agent center Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are at an impasse this season and the franchise is uncertain if he will show up to next Monday's Media Day, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

"When you talk to people close to [Duren], he feels a certain way toward the Pistons' respect level for him," Charania said on NBA Today. "For him it's been all about respect, for the team it has just been about business. ... Over the course of this offseason, his offer has been been around the $180 to $190 million over five years range. And that has also included incentives like weight clauses to my understanding. And that has all played a part in this as well.

"Over the last several weeks it's kind of quiet on this front. The sides have picked up communication. And I am told right now the Pistons offer to Jalen Duren is $200 million over five years."

Duren has until Oct. 1 to sign a qualifying offer.

Hawks' Henri Veesaar out with torn ACL

The Atlanta Hawks announced that center Henri Veesaar tore his ACL during a Sept. 15 workout. He will undergo surgery in October and is expected to miss the entire 2026-27 season.

Sept. 18

Pistons, Thompson reach five-year, $155 million extension

Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN.

Thompson lands the fully guaranteed extension after making first-team All-Defense and finishing third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season. The 23-year-old averaged 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 0.9 blocks in 2025-26 while leading the NBA in steals per game (2.0).

articles.headline: Nicolas Batum announces retirement after 18 NBA seasons
articles.description: Nicolas Batum has announced his retirement after 18 NBA seasons. A mainstay of the French national team, Batum played most of his NBA career with the Clippers, Hornets and Blazers.
articles.body:
Nicolas Batum, a longtime NBA forward and stalwart for France's national team, announced his retirement Monday in a social media video with his son.

"Yeah, that's it," Batum said. "Dad's done playing basketball. I've been playing for a long time. ... Twenty years as a pro. That's a lot. Eighteen years in the NBA. Fifteen with the French national team. ... It's over."

Batum, 37, spent most of the past six seasons with the LA Clippers, including averaging 4.0 points and 2.5 rebounds per game in 74 appearances last season. The 2008 first-round pick entered the NBA as a teenager and spent his first seven seasons with the Portland Trail Blazers before a lengthy stint with the Charlotte Hornets and a brief stop with the Philadelphia 76ers during the 2023-24 season.

Prior to joining the NBA, Batum played two seasons in the French league.

"I decided to retire from basketball for several reasons," Batum told his 10-year-old son, Ayden, in the video. "I want to come home and be with you. I'm going to take care of you and make room for others. I think I've done my time. My time with France ended two years ago. And the NBA is over too. You know, when you've played as much basketball as I have, at some point, you have to know when to stop. ... I've done everything I needed to do."

A versatile forward capable of defending multiple positions and stretching opposing defenses with his outside shot, Batum posted career averages of 9.6 points, 4.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game while shooting 37.1% on 3-pointers. During his career, Batum appeared in 76 playoff games and reached the 2021 Western Conference finals with the Clippers.

The native of Lisieux, France, was deeply committed to representing his country on the international stage, competing with longtime teammates Rudy Gobert and Evan Fournier. Batum started for French teams that won silver medals at the 2020 and 2024 Olympics, he won bronze medals at the 2014 and 2019 FIBA World Cups, and he medaled at the 2011, 2013 and 2015 EuroBasket tournaments.

Batum said in the video that France's semifinal win over Germany at the 2024 Olympics in Paris was "the best basketball moment I've ever experienced."

Earlier this summer, the Clippers declined their option on Batum's $5.9 million contract for the 2026-27 season, leaving him as an unrestricted free agent.
